communityVoices.quote: the best Morning Dew of the year in an incredible Dew year (2/24,3/23,6/18,9/10). Yes it's the one in the the movie, and for my ears, perhaps the best all-time performance - totally tight, zero mistakes, huge power from Phil, incredible dynamics, perfect!
It's filled with energy and emotion and the solo sections are absolutely nuts. This is THE Dew.
This show really stands on it's own. It is the most ''acoustic'' electric show ! have heard from '74. The sound is super intimate and i love it. Vocals WAY out front.
it evolves into a funky feel reminiscent of jazz-rock of the same period
Though it fails me, I cannot recall anything special about the night's music.

whyThisShow: This is one of the October 1974 Winterland farewell-run nights captured for the Grateful Dead Movie, and the community treats it as canonical, anchored almost entirely to the Morning Dew. One reviewer called it "perhaps the best all-time performance - totally tight, zero mistakes, huge power from Phil, incredible dynamics, perfect" [source: 'perhaps the best all-time performance - totally tight, zero mistakes, huge power from Phil, incredible dynamics, perfect!']. Another seconded that the Dew "is what makes this show so special" and that "the solo sections are absolutely nuts" [source: 'the Morning Dew is what makes this show so special. It's filled with energy and emotion and the solo sections are absolutely nuts']. The second set as a whole draws its own praise: one listener called it "one of most unique sets ever" and "a complete meltdown" [source: 'the second set is one of most unique sets ever. As stated earlier, a complete meltdown']. One attendee who was there in person does note that despite a magnificent recording, "I cannot recall anything special about the night's music" [source: 'I cannot recall anything special about the night's music'], a minority view in a pool of five-star reverence.
listenFor: The path through the second set is where this one earns its reputation: the jam that flows into Dark Star is described as "genius" and the Dark Star itself as "not a spacy, indulgent Dark Star, but a seemingly well-crafted musical Dark Star, with very smooth transitions, and a mellow feel throughout" [source: 'not a spacy, indulgent Dark Star, but a seemingly well-crafted musical Dark Star, with very smooth transitions, and a mellow feel throughout']. That Dark Star then takes a left turn where "it evolves into a funky feel reminiscent of jazz-rock of the same period" [source: 'it evolves into a funky feel reminiscent of jazz-rock of the same period']. Then comes the Dew. One reviewer also flagged that the recording carries an unusual sonic character: "the most 'acoustic' electric show I have heard from '74" with "Vocals WAY out front" [source: 'the most ''acoustic'' electric show ! have heard from '74. The sound is super intimate and i love it. Vocals WAY out front']. The soundboard source here comes from Jay Ashley, and one attendee noted "a slight anomaly in my ears to the drums" that is audible on the recording but that "does not spoil the overall effect" [source: 'a slight anomaly in my ears to the drums. As I listen to this recording now I can hear it, but it does not spoil the overall effect'].
context: This show falls in the wall-of-sound era, one night into the legendary October 1974 Winterland run that served as the Dead's pre-hiatus farewell to performing. The recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd74-10-18.sbd.bertha-ashley.22796.sbeok.shnf), sourced from Jay Ashley. Footage and audio from this run were used in the Grateful Dead Movie, released as part of the October 16–20, 1974 film documentation. One reviewer singled out Donna's performance as being "on" that night, noting "even Donna is on" [source: 'even Donna is on, but the jam->Dark Star->Dew is one for the ages'].
funFact: One reviewer who attended in person walked straight past security without presenting a ticket — "I walked straight into the main floor and essentially right on up to the front of the stage. It was not at all crowded" — and spent the night clean, no substances, head clear [source: 'I walked straight into the main floor and essentially right on up to the front of the stage. It was not at all crowded'].
headline: Phil's Dew, Winterland, October '74.
